entities.summary: Avitus of Braga was a powerful entrepreneur and religious leader of the Visigothic Kingdom in the 5th century CE. He played a crucial role in shaping the kingdom's political and religious landscape. Avitus of Braga was born in the late 4th century CE, but the exact date of his birth is unknown. He died in 440 CE, leaving behind a legacy that influenced the Visigothic Kingdom for centuries. Avitus of Braga was a key figure in the kingdom's transition to Christianity, and his efforts helped to establish the Catholic Church in the Visigothic Kingdom. He also played a significant role in the kingdom's military campaigns, leading the Visigoths to several victories against the Romans. Avitus of Braga's leadership and diplomacy helped to secure the Visigothic Kingdom's borders and establish trade relationships with neighboring kingdoms. His legacy extended beyond the Visigothic Kingdom, as he was recognized by the Roman Emperor Theodosius II as a prominent religious leader. Avitus of Braga's impact on the development of Christianity in the 5th century CE is still studied by historians today. His commitment to the Catholic Church and his role in shaping the Visigothic Kingdom's religious landscape make him a significant figure in the history of Western Christianity.
